{{nihongo|'''Taniya Shrine'''|多爾夜神社|Taniya-jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Arari, {{ill|Nishiizu|arz|نيشيزو|ceb|Nishiizu Chō|es|Nishiizu (Shizuoka)|fa|نیشی‌ایزو|fr|Nishiizu|id|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|it|Nishiizu|ja|西伊豆町|ko|니시이즈정|ms|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|pl|Nishiizu|ru|Нисиидзу|tl|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|tr|Nishiizu|uk|Нісі-Ідзу|ur|نیشی اوزو|vi|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|zh|西伊豆町|zh_yue|西伊豆町|qid=Q1203949}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|Q961511|qid=Q961511}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}, Japan. It is listed in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]] as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and was historically part of [[Izu Province]]. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|en|Kotoshironushi|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611}} and held the rank of {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} in the modern shrine ranking system. The shrine is known for its annual Sarumai (monkey dance) festival held on November 3.

'''Taniya Shrine''' (たにやじんじゃ)<ref>[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4401180 多爾夜神社] - Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines</ref> is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Arari, {{ill|Nishiizu|arz|نيشيزو|ceb|Nishiizu Chō|es|Nishiizu (Shizuoka)|fa|نیشی‌ایزو|fr|Nishiizu|id|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|it|Nishiizu|ja|西伊豆町|ko|니시이즈정|ms|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|pl|Nishiizu|ru|Нисиидзу|tl|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|tr|Nishiizu|uk|Нісі-Ідзу|ur|نیشی اوزو|vi|Nishiizu, Shizuoka|zh|西伊豆町|zh_yue|西伊豆町|qid=Q1203949}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|Q961511|qid=Q961511}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is one of the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|ja|伊豆国の式内社一覧|qid=Q11380552}}.

== Overview ==
Its foundation is unknown, but as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} it dates back to before {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), when the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' was compiled<ref>[https://kotobank.jp/word/神名帳-82644 神名帳とは] - {{ill|Kotobank|Q11302260|qid=Q11302260}}</ref>.

The shrine name is said to derive from “Taniya,” and Yama Shrine up the mountain path in the same district is said to be the original shrine.

At the annual festival on November 3, together with nearby Dezaki Shrine, children in red costumes perform the Sarumai (Sarukko dance)<ref name="kk">[https://www.nishiizu-kankou.com/sightseeing/taniyasarumai 多爾夜神社猿舞] - Nishiizu Tourism Association</ref><ref name="act-jt">[http://odoriko.act-jt.jp/report.pdf Izu regional folk performing arts] - ACTJT</ref>.

== Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsumuha-yae Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}

== Precincts ==
* Memorial monument to the war dead
* Wasureji-no-hi monument - erected in {{ill|1975|Q2479|qid=Q2479}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 50) by former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yokaren}} trainees (naval youth aviators) in gratitude for local residents’ kindness<ref>[https://www.nishiizu-kankou.com/sightseeing/wasurejinoto Wasureji Monument] - Nishiizu Tourism Association</ref>.

== Sarumai (Sarukko dance) ==
There are several origin theories, but all share that it contains prayers related to fishing<ref name="kk"/><ref name="act-jt"/>. The program consists of:
# Standing dance
# Fan dance
# Handstand dance
# Whale-spearing dance
four performances in total<ref name="kk"/><ref name="act-jt"/>.

Originally danced solo by young men, but after local youth groups disappeared, when the dance was revived in {{ill|1980|Q2439|qid=Q2439}} (Shōwa 55), elementary school children began performing it as a group<ref name="act-jt"/>.
